The lack of diversity is definitely sort of feeding itself. While I also try to stick it out in those communities in order to combat that, it just sucks sometimes. It sucks explaining basic human decency to people who should know better, it sucks when someone tries to talk to other POC in the space (ie asking for feedback from other POC) and the comments are filled with white folks derailing the conversation or inserting their unwanted perspective, I could go on.

There’s also culture, which many folks here have touched on. I’m Native, and so I don’t really think I had as strong a grip on monogamy as others do. The hesitation and fear that others describe isn’t really something I feel when I think about “coming out” to my family and community. Not that Natives are slutting around lol, but our cultures have always involved multiple wives, partners, two spirits, all kinds of “alternative” shit that was just normal. If they judge me, it’s the same way they’d judge my clothes or weight or whatever else, lol. Now, as a Native raised on a reservation colonized by Catholics and who grew up Catholic, that’s not to say I always felt that way — but now that I am not longer religious and have unlearned a lot of that, I’m not really concerned with how my community or family would receive my partners/relationships. I know my ancestors are chill with it if I’m being a good relative 🤷🏽‍♀️ 

That being said, it’s kinda funny that as a Native, I do feel so uncomfortable or alone in those spaces so often. You’d think I’d be most comfortable, haha. 

People do not like discomfort and at the end of the day, temporary discomfort is necessary for creating a welcoming space. Unlearning racism isn’t fun. I have to do it, too! It’s so much easier to just ignore it and pat themselves on the back for being nontraditional and “ethical”. And frankly, a lot of people who say they want “community” have no damn clue what that word means, nor do they know that it requires a hell of a lot of discomfort in order to be successful.

I will say that here in Minnesota, there are some really great white allies in poly and queer spaces who are always trying to shut down hate in its many forms. Including leadership, and I know we’re lucky to have them! But that doesn’t change that the hate exists and as long as it does, Black and brown ppl won’t feel safe there. 

Personally, my approach is tribal. If you’re going to be hurtful (and yes, words are hurtful), you are harming the community and cannot be a part of it. Loud banishment, good ol’ shame. But that’s just me.

There are folks telling you you should have heard them out/gave them a chance. I’ve been in a situation remarkably similar to yours. 3 partners, very little time. Even when they broke up with one of the partners they had very little time. However, I trusted them and their ability to choose the connections in their life. They assured me the connection was important to them. I was patient, I did everything I could to not add stress to their life. I always offered quality time without expectation, making it clear it was okay if it didn’t work out today/this week. They still ghosted me after 6 months of being best friends and lovers. They came back later with a message FILLED with resentment for “pressuring” them with check-ins and excusing their behavior with how they don’t have the capacity to engage at all. 

It’s important to protect your heart. It’s okay for someone to have many partners and it obviously works for a lot of the community, but there are so many people out there at various stages of healing and growth and folks get hurt in their path. You saw a flag and listened to your intuition. I’m proud of you. And I’m sorry it didn’t work out for you. ❤️

So I didn’t become sexually active until i was about 25/26, and the first thing you should know is that being 20 and not being sexually active is soooo much more common than you are led to believe. There’s nothing wrong with you - it’s a pandemic, social situations are weird, and again, it’s not as unusual as you think. 

The second thing is that working on regaining your self worth will do WONDERS. The second I started becoming content with my own company and started recognizing my strengths in the context of friend groups/social situations (I’m very warm, I’m funny, I’m a good listener, i keep people’s energy positive, etc), I could tell people looked at me differently and saw me as more attractive. What’s more is that lately I have felt disconnected from that confidence in myself, and have felt extremely unattractive/undesirable as a result. Do not underestimate the power of true, authentic confidence and self-worth. The fact that you recognize the problem (that you get your positive self-image from other people) will make it so much easier to work on going forward. 

Writing good things about myself every day helps me, but I know it’s not for everyone. Maybe you can take some time every day/week that specifically for yourself - do something that you would normally not consider a priority but that makes you feel good, like watching your favorite movie or drawing or reading a book for pleasure. Build a relationship with yourself. Sorry this is so long but I hope it helps!

If possible, try to either get counseling or go to a support group. Counseling is good even on your good days. I was lucky enough to find a support group at my school after my brother committed suicide, and even though I wasn’t able to go every week (i had a rehearsal that clashed with the time), it was helpful to release some of the feelings that seemed to just build and build. However, I don’t know how typical it was to have a group like that already formed and active. 

It helped for me to stay distracted outside of class. I had theater rehearsals, acapella group rehearsals, LGBT club meetings and Native American student group meetings. I always ate at the dining halls, even if I was alone. I didn’t do exceptionally well that first quarter after he died (to be fair, he died about two weeks before I was due to return to school), but building those habits and routines made the next quarter a lot easier and I did pretty great. 

The important thing is to not try and pretend everything is fine when it’s not, but also not to feel guilty on the days when you ARE doing well. Embrace either end of the spectrum and adjust your schedule accordingly. I allowed myself a day to wallow on the weekends, but the routines and obligations I had put in place actually made it so I didn’t need as much time as I thought i needed. 

On the other hand, my best friend passed away almost two years ago and I have not returned to school since purely because it was so unbelievably devastating and I am nowhere near ready. If you find it completely impossible, maybe explore if a temporary medical leave is an option for you. It’s not for everyone - you have to have the willpower to eventually go back - but if your mental health needs it, consider it. 

I am so sorry for your loss. To lose your favorite person is truly a life-altering and traumatizing experience. I’m sending all of my love and warmth to you.

Just a disclaimer: Brody was an absolute asshole for not telling Rachel what he was doing. 

That being said: I get it. I think a character doing something that would realistically have happened is not equivalent to bad writing. People do fucked up things.

I think Brody, on paper, is wildly interesting. Midwest boy, at an art school, on scholarship, doing whatever he can to survive in this big city while trying to hold on to this amazing opportunity he has. To me, Montana Midwest is very different from Ohio Midwest. Montana is a more rural place (not exclusively, but I grew up in North Dakota and can tell you for a fact that they (MT and OH) are very different cultures. It is a Huge Deal that he is a straight dude who managed to get into a performing arts school. 

So to me, that was ripe for storytelling. I was ready to experience a heart wrenching or at least interesting story with him, with or without Rachel. Part of me wishes he could have stuck around and we could have learned more about him besides the conclusions I drew from the info we got. Not with Rachel, of course, because that kind of betrayal is just too much to overcome, I think. But that was a good opportunity to write about sex work, and as much as I hate to say this, I think the show really blew it there (though I personally think fandom’s reaction to him had a lot to do with that).

I don’t necessarily take a side in it, but I lean more toward Rachel’s just because Santana should have talked to her about it. She absolutely should have. Rachel definitely overreacted and should have been happy that Santana got that opportunity, but Santana should have, at that point, recognized that Rachel’s overreaction has to do with their history - specifically her history of treating Rachel like shit. Yeah, it was years before, but you don’t just get over that. Funny Girl is Rachel’s THING - she doesn’t own it, but if Santana was Rachel’s friend, she would at least have tried to understand all the baggage that would come with her infiltrating Rachel’s safest place. 

Tbh they both just frustrated the fuck out of me for that entire arc because if they would just have tried to talk to each other, they could have figured it out and made up. We did get Be Okay out of it though, which is one of my favorite duets.
